tasks.behavior: Implement hosted and origin-restricted embedded checkout
acceptance: Hosted integration works without a browser package; full and element embeds reuse trusted checkout and support existing payment lifecycles.
Only configured exact origins can frame an embed; normal pay pages remain unframeable; loopback HTTP is test-only and live returns require HTTPS.

tasks.behavior: Build minimal JavaScript and React checkout packages
acceptance: Browser packages provide PayButton, Checkout and PaymentElement over existing checkout URLs, without secret keys or client-authoritative financial state.
Typed messages verify origin/source and mount lifecycle cleans listeners; React 18 and 19 compatibility, type/build/size and packed-install checks pass.

tasks.behavior: Prove merchant checkout fulfillment and reconciliation end to end
acceptance: The example merchant prices a cart on its server, creates real checkouts, verifies events and fulfills an order once across hosted and embedded flows.
Independent shared-link customers, client invoicing, multi-store isolation, expiration, partial payment, delivery recovery and spoofed prices/messages have automated workflow coverage.
Ledger/export totals reconcile against receiver and wallet chain balances; duplicate/reordered events cannot double-fulfill.
Quickstart and integration docs match implemented packages; provider limitations, actual user testing and release approvals are reported truthfully.

tasks.behavior: Recover payment processing and enforce revocation and webhook fairness
acceptance: Incomplete RPC logs never create permanent conflicts; previously affected deposits recover only after exact canonical evidence is verified.
Large verified deposit backlogs make bounded durable progress, preserve exact allocation and event semantics, and settle without duplicate booking. Invoice creation and expiry use one timestamp.
Role changes recheck current actor permissions under the profile lock, preventing pending requests from undoing a demotion.
Webhook test and resend work has bounded tenant budgets; slow tenants cannot occupy every sender slot or starve other profiles.

tasks.behavior: Asset values use shared market prices for USDC, USDT and Open USD
acceptance: The worker stores CoinGecko prices every 15 minutes and GET /v1/prices returns them with staleness
Holdings show market USD values at the latest known price, name no price provider, and never fall back to 1 USD
notes: 2026-10-29 review pass by independent-reviewer: Pass. Accept 1 holds. config.go:86 sets DefaultPricesEvery to 15 minutes, and cmd/worker/main.go:82 and :104 tick the keeper with it. TestKeeperReadsWhenDue reads at the first tick and again only after the interval. It retries 2 minutes after a failure and keeps a coin's last price when an answer has none. TestListGivesEachEnabledTokenItsCoinPrice gives a test token its mainnet coin's price and marks old reads stale. TestPrices (httpapi/tests/prices_test.go:11) returns usd, sourceUpdatedAt, fetchedAt and stale for any signed-in user, and null before any read. Accept 2 holds. Holdings values (balance-figure.tsx, balances-screen.tsx, balances-list.tsx, assets-card.tsx, business-overview.tsx) go through marketUsd or latestUsd and usdCents in features/prices/lib/prices.ts. Those value exact base units at the latest price, even a stale one, and return null without a price. The two named web tests exist; balances and prices unit tests pass (16 of 16). In apps/web/src and packages the provider is named only in two comments in features/prices/schemas/prices.ts:4 and :10, in no text users see. Notes, not blocking: (1) the doc comment at features/balances/lib/balances.ts:11-12 sits above settling, not marketUsd, and says 'no fresh price', but the code uses stale prices. (2) The balance history chart, its change figure and the received and sent totals still count each stablecoin as 1 USD (balance/history.go:22-23, openapi estimatedUsd). So the chart's last point can differ by cents from the market-value total beside it. This is by design, not a fallback, but the owner may want to decide it. (3) on-its-way-card.tsx:39 and :90 show 0.00 for a part that has no price when the other part has one.

tasks.behavior: A chain's payment scan keeps moving when an RPC limits requests
acceptance: A log range or batch one endpoint refuses goes to the next endpoint; the scan narrows only when no endpoint takes it, and grows back after accepted queries
Endpoints are chosen by measured answer time and failure share, not by name; private endpoints stay first
Each scan records what it read within 60% of its deadline and always moves the cursor, so a slow or narrow provider cannot stall a chain
The worker logs an ALERT for a stalled chain, a deposit stuck as detected, and paid money not settled in time or near its deadline
notes:
2026-10-29 review pass by independent-reviewer: PASS. Both blocking findings from the F350 review are fixed. (1) docs/tasks.json now only adds F351 and sets nextId 351 to 352; F343, F344 and F347-F350 match HEAD 7e5b37b8. (2) rpc.md:56-57 now match the code: a refusing endpoint is ranked last for that size for an hour (pool.go:262-263), and the refusal reaches the caller only when no other endpoint answered (pool.go:133-135, 178-180).
Fixes checked: alerts.go only alerts intents whose settle deadline is still ahead, and alerts_test adds a past-deadline intent that must stay silent. TestBatchOneEndpointRefusesGoesToTheNext (pool_test.go:602) sends a 5-call batch past a 3-call endpoint and checks the refusal is remembered; the old pool returned the first refusal, so it fails there. post() measures only usable answers and size refusals (pool.go:474, 506). refused() sets refusedAt only when it records a size and ignores single-block refusals (pool.go:192-209). scanRange records when from > latest (watcher.go:122): latest becomes from-1, the cursor cannot pass the node finalized block (record keeps the greatest), and a recovery sweep with target below next completes. This also fixes a case the earlier version had: a new chain whose finalized block equals latest (Tempo, Arc) got from = finalized+1 > latest, so the first Scan never created its cursor.
Re-run: changed pool tests with -race, TestAlerts, and the watcher range, backlog, growth, slow-provider and Recover tests all pass. harness verify passed at 17:48:55Z, after the last source edit (17:48:42Z). docs-check 0 errors; no added doc sentence over 25 words.
Non-blocking: (a) rpc.md:51 says an endpoint unused for 10 minutes costs nothing; since failures no longer update usedAt, an endpoint that only failed for 10 minutes also costs nothing and is tried first after each rest (a hanging one costs up to 5 s per try). Say: without a usable answer for 10 minutes. (b) Unchanged by agreement: a refusal during the health probe counts as a size refusal (pool.go:157-166); the overlap is min(2000, span), so with a narrowed span recovery is the only second look; a failed pending-row re-read (watcher.go:164-166) drops the main progress, and a started range can run past the 60% mark. (c) No test covers the first Scan of a chain whose finalized block equals latest.

tasks.behavior: Payments book from the chain-wide scan without per-receiver evidence
acceptance: The chain's scan records deposits and each receiver's settle, refund and recover events at the finalized block; no per-receiver scan, proof or coverage gate remains, and its tables are dropped

The ledger books deposits and receiver events in chain order; paid still needs the finalized balanceOf to cover every booked deposit; an event the balances can't cover, or found after later movements, stays unbooked with its reason
The signer records its own settle from the finalized, canonical receipt and books it at once; it refuses to sign while the finalized balance is below the booked receiver balance
Payment API reads keep their shape; a caught-up worker round makes no RPC calls that grow with paid invoices
